title: Standard-Model Security for Derived-Key Transformations
summary: The derived-key transformation is readily provable secure in the random-oracle model, while a formal standard-model security treatment remains open.

formal_statement.body: Develop a formal standard-model security treatment for the key-derivation approach in which a transformed scheme $\Gamma(\Pi)$, with key $K$, uses the internal scheme $\Pi$ under the derived key $K' = H(\tau,K)$, where $H$ is a hash function and $\tau$ is an input parameter. The transformation is readily provable secure in the random-oracle model, but a formal treatment in the standard model remains open.

scope.domain: Standard-model security analysis of a hash-based key-derivation transformation for authenticated encryption.
parameters: K: key of the transformed scheme
K′: derived key used internally with Π
τ: input parameter to the key derivation
H: hash function deriving K′ from τ and K
scope.unresolved_remainder: Develop a formal security treatment of the key-derivation transformation in the standard model.

progress.summary: The source presents random-oracle security as readily provable and explicitly leaves the corresponding formal standard-model treatment as an open problem.
citation_labels: Reza Reyhanitabar et al., Authenticated Encryption with Variable Stretch
